newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler praises German tax reform plans.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler praises German tax reform plans.

text.p: Senior Bundesbank official Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Thursday hailed Germany's pension reform plans as a major coup, which could be instrumental in reviving sluggish German economic growth.

If political parties agree on the plan's fundamental components, then the plan could be seen to support German economic growth even in the current year, Zeitler told German daily Sueddeutsche Zeitung in an interview.
Zeitler, also president of the state central bank in Bavaria, said a planned reduction of tax rates as well as a noticable reduction of tax burdens were such key elements.
If the proposals were agreed upon, investment activity could pick up, Zeitler told the newspaper.
Companies could benefit from higher write-offs in 1997 and 1998 but would only have to pay reduced taxes on the profits received through investments in 1999.
This could support growth projections, he said.
Zeitler said Germany's tax system would become internationally more competitive if top tax rates for individuals were around 39 percent and top rates for companies were around 35 percent.

Zeitler explained that expanded M3 money supply, which includes deposits at foreign banks, had recently grown less rapidly than narrow M3, which includes cash in circulation, and short-term savings deposits.
Lower tax rates could prompt people to invest money in Germany, pulling it back from other countries.
